newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs up, after falling on large-lot hedge selling.
newsitem.headline: JGBs up, after falling on large-lot hedge selling.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was slightly higher by midday on Monday, due to the Bank of Japan's outright bond buying operation in the morning, traders said.

The central bank's offer to buy 100 billion yen in bonds outright in an agreement starting on May 2, caught many in the market by surprise and led to buy backs of JGBs, a senior city bank trader said.
"Although some purchases of JGBs were seen right before the BOJ's bond buying, the operation had a reassuring effect on the market and gave JGBs a boost," the trader said.
Earlier, there was speculation that the BOJ may reduce its outright purchases of JGBs. It has been buying about 200 billion yen worth of JGBs each month since January.

There was little immediate impact from the Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Washington, but its call for Japan to achieve strong domestic demand-led growth may temper rises in JGBs in the long run, traders said.

"Japan seems to have made an international commitment to increase domestic demand at the G7. This could keep hitting JGBs like blows to the body, and have a negative impact on the bond market," a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
The June stood at 125.59 by midday, up slightly from Friday's close of 125.50. Turnover was 25,142 contracts.

Those who have been behind the recent large-lot buying of June JGB futures put options with a strike price of 123.00, may be speculating that Japan will be forced to increase fiscal spending to stimulate the economy, the first trader said.

"Hedge funds who are rumoured to be behind the buying of the put options, may be speculating that Japan will reconsider its public investment plans in order to achieve the objectives outlined by the G7," he said.

Foreign speculators apparently have not liquidated their long positions on the 123.00 June JGB futures put options despite a sharp rise in the premium on Friday. They are rumoured to be still holding 123.00-yen put options with a theoretical value of about one trillion yen, the trader said.
The premium on the June JGB futures put options with a strike price of 123.00 stood at 0.21 by midday on Monday, up from Friday's close of 0.20.
The premium had stood at 0.07 at Thursday's close.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.270 percent as of 0256 GMT, up slightly from Friday's close of 2.265 percent.
Traders said investors were taking a wait-and-see stance after the G7 and ahead of a national holiday on Tuesday.
Investors showed scant appetite for long-term and super long-term JGBs in the morning, a trader at a long-term credit bank's securities unit said.
However a rumour that some buying of the 194th 10-year JGB had been detected lent support to the market, the first trader said.
The market would be watching March industrial output data due at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), traders said.
